2. Per-site rG (G_j = all downstream reader Grams, C_j = the site's own moment + ridge 1e-3), clip_self, quick.
- Known-answer check: the glob mode (one basis at every site, own forward with skip maps) reproduces r2_p6_rG_rho exactly (.7: 3.123 / 27.5%). f = 1 gives KL .000.

- b0 3.156 / 27.5%. The real rG row is 3.123 / 27.5%, so the check passes. b = 0 at f = 1 gives KL .000.
- b3 3.013 / 27.5%, b6 1.970 / 43.5%, b9 .776 / 66.0%, b12 .000 / 100%.
- My prediction of an even spread failed. When blocks 3-11 are already cut, also cutting blocks 0-2 adds only .14 KL. Blocks 3-5 add 1.04, blocks 6-8 add 1.19, and blocks 9-11 plus the readout add .78.
- This is a conditional reading (cut from block b on). b12 shows only that the ln_post divisor costs nothing. The readout projection sits inside the b9 row and is not isolated.

findings:
F1. Why the fold hurt the whole CLIP cut. Expected: the fold collides with the stream cut. Happened, quick, 200 photos:
- Heads + MLP cut, stream full: the fold helps at .85. Off is 3.527 / 29.0%, fold is 1.920 / 45.0%. At .95 they tie (.380 / 78.5% vs .365 / 75.0%; critic paired z -1.46).
- Stream + MLP cut, heads full: the fold hurts. Off is .451 / 81.5% and 5.097 / 18.5%. Fold is .638 / 71.5% and 4.816 / 9.5%.
- Full rows confirm it: -6.5 agree at .95 and -6.1 at .85.
So the collision is with the FLOOR-COORDINATE stream cut, not with the heads. With JOINT's rG stream the fold helps (JOINT: leaving it out costs 12 agree).

F2. The cause. On the same stream + MLP cut, quick:
- Open loop: .386 / 75.0% and 2.384 / 39.5%.
- kslice (kept rows of G reset to the slice, only the cut units' message folded): .353 / 80.0% and 2.219 / 40.0%.
- Fold moments on the clip_self input: .562 / 72.5% and 4.488 / 14.5%. This does not fix the fold, so I dropped the input idea.
The harm is the closed-loop REMAP of the kept units' own write columns. In the closed loop those columns absorb the stream-cut damage seen on X. Why that remap is wrong on photos is open. Pink is not shown to be the cause, because the self input does not help.
kslice was picked on quick photos. The 800 unseen photos hold (critic and my paired reads).

F3. Whole cut, full run:
- Off .820 / 68.2% and 7.737 / 5.1%.
- kslice .628 / 71.4% and 4.058 / 21.0%.
- Roll null .694 / 69.9% and 4.785 / 17.4%.
- Against off: .95 KL -.192 +- .020, agree +3.2 (z 2.9). .85 KL -3.679, agree +15.9 (z 11.8).
- Against the null: .95 is a tie on agree (z 1.6). .85 has +3.6 agree (z 3.7) and KL -.726 +- .044.
- At .85 most of the gain is form (the null gets 12.3 of the 15.9 points).
So the floor coordinates plus kslice take the whole CLIP 85% off chance with no rG stream.

F4. MLP-only, full run. Fold against off and null:
- .7: 2.513 / 37.6% vs off 6.694 / 9.9% and null 5.096 / 14.1%.
- .5: 6.223 / 7.0% vs off .2% and null 1.7%. The KL is at the flat level.

F5. The output-weighted error. Algebra: a stream metric M = sum g_r r r^T cancels for an unconstrained write, because M(W' Ss - W Sx) = 0 gives the same G. So M can act only through sample weights, the ridge, or the stream-cut left factor. The cheap case, CLS-token rows weighted 196 (r3_write_m_cls), gave quick .85 .706 / 69.5%. Off (r2_p4_wfold_mlp quick, TREE's r3_tree_off) is .791 / 65.0%. That is +4.5 agree, unpaired, picked on quick photos: a lead only.
Related evidence: kslice by construction has a larger least-squares residual on X than the plain fold, yet it wins on photos. This is direct evidence that the least-squares stream error is not the KL target, as VECMATH 8 says. The g_r metric itself was not built.

findings:
Scope: CLIP, MLP-only, 85%. The kept set is the magcut weight order. Every row uses plain deletion plus the P4 fold (slice anchor, closed loop), solved again after the tilt. Input: pink n256. Photo use: test photos for scoring only. I picked no knob on the held split, because no rule beat off.

1. Fixed tilt toward the top fold partner.
- Expected: f10 gains +1 to +3 agree over off.
- Happened (quick): off .791 / 65.0%, f05 .853 / 64.5%, f10 1.021 / 62.0%.
- Happened (full): off .776 / 66.8%, f10 .971 / 64.2%.
- The harm grows steadily with tilt size from 0. I did not run f20.

2. Random-partner null.
- Expected: rand10 about the same as f10.
- Happened: rand10 quick .937 / 65.5%, full .931 / 64.3%.
- So the fold partner does MORE harm than a random partner (full: +.04 KL, the same agree).

3. Why. A scale error is refuted.
- With renorm (tilted pre-activation reset to the unit's own mean and sd): f10r .979 / 62.5%, rand10r .930 / 66.5%.
- The sd moved only 2-3%.
- The real cause is a hub pick. On raw G, blocks 8-10 have only 94-146 distinct partners for 2,611 kept units. The top partner owns 18-23% of the kept units, so many reads move along ONE shared direction. Random partners give 460 distinct partners, about 1% each.
- I divided each G row by the cut unit's firing rms (n10). This gave 264-390 distinct partners. Quick: .858 / 65.5% against f10's 1.021 / 62.0%, so most of the extra harm goes away. It is still above off in KL.

4. R1 partner, from weights only.
- 29-57% of kept units have a cut unit with the same parent.
- r10r: quick .859 / 63.0%, full .900 / 64.9%.
- This is the best of the tilts, but it is still worse than off by .12 KL and 1.9 agree (full).

5. The LEAD 17:01 form. Each cut unit tilts only its top carrier (score = |beta| / the partner's total |beta| mass), with renorm, then refold. 206-398 units are tilted per block.
- Quick: one10 .797 / 65.5%, its null oneperm .797 / 64.0%, off .791 / 65.0%.
- This is a three-way tie. My prediction (beats its null by >= .02 KL) failed.

6. Calculated descent tilt (g10). Each read takes one step along the gradient of the block's write residual ||D(aT - G aS)||^2 on pink, at .1 sd per unit.
- Derived from: the same least squares as the fold, with its gradient taken with respect to the reads. It is not the tree rule.
- The local residual went down (mean over blocks .051, against rand10 .058).
- It is the worst row: quick 1.346 / 60.5%. A step that lowers a block-local objective on pink does not carry over to photos.
- |cos| between this direction and the top-fold-partner read is higher than for a random cut read in blocks 1-3 and 9-10 (block 9: .42 against .25). Elsewhere it ties the unit's own read. This is weak support for VECMATH 11's direction on raw G, and that G is hub-biased.

Reading: at 85% on pink, a read tilt of a fixed size (toward a fold, R1, random or calculated partner) never beats plain deletion plus fold. The harm gets smaller as the tilt spreads over more partners. The best tilts only tie off. All quick agree gaps are 2-7 photos out of 200. The full rows (n = 1,000) set the order: off .776/66.8 > r10r .900/64.9 > rand10 .931/64.3 > f10 .971/64.2.
